question: Did the Google Docs suggestion audit omit any material behavior or platform contract, and do those omissions change its architecture verdict?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; redesign-from-first-principles; Blast Radius safety-fact crosswalk; three-candidate Arena omission challenge with independent cross-judge; Technical Writing evidence repair
trigger: After the first Google Docs behavior audit, the user explicitly requested a second pass to make sure nothing material was missed.
requirements: Challenge the audit independently across content, structure, format, review, lifecycle, interop, accessibility, and scale.
Distinguish observed Google UI behavior, official documentation/schema, current repository evidence, and inference; do not treat a schema field as live UI proof.
Map every current Google Docs request union member to an explicit Google-facing family or unsupported/deferred disposition.
Map every earlier F01-F32 native-authored contract to the corrected denominator so platform laws cannot disappear inside broad Google-operation rows.
Preserve the audit-first boundary: correct research artifacts and immutable review history without changing product code, running another performance trial, or mutating the supplied Google document.
Reconsider restoration, a second suggestion store, native ownership, and the semantic review boundary in light of every material omission.
evidenceReuse: Reused the original 25 Chrome probes without new Google document mutations and preserved their one-author, online, macOS limits. Re-read the current official Requests, Document, suggest-write/thread/update-status, and screen-reader sources. Three independent read-only challengers inspected the original audit against official schemas, current Plate/Plite producers and consumers, and F01-F32; a fourth read-only agent cross-judged all candidates. The parent reconciled accepted findings into a machine-readable 48-request and 32-contract crosswalk and verified its counts and family references locally.
summary: Supersede the first audit's 32-family completeness boundary with 44 selected families: 37 Google-facing and seven Plate/Plite platform/lifecycle families. Reaffirm one native authored owner and the cut of kind-plus-ranges as the sole review contract. The target must also cover producer group cardinality and outcomes, author withdrawal, durable closed review provenance, global scopes, live paging recovery, and explicit AI/external-text/anchor/retention/codec/lifetime laws.
alternatives: Keep the first 32-family denominator: reject. It omits official request/schema scopes and current Plate/Plite producers, persistence, anchors, and mounted lifetime contracts.
Expand one broad Google matrix until it absorbs all platform laws: reject. Google interaction families and local lifecycle invariants need separate but cross-mapped denominators.

Restore the removed Suggestion mutation engine or add a second suggestion store: reject. None of the omitted behaviors gives duplicate identity, mutation, decision, or persistence authority an independent user job.

Keep native authored ownership while extending the review read/outcome boundary and Plate workflow: pursue. Add global targets, provenance, producer outcomes, durable discussion linkage, capabilities, stale paging, and partial-failure recovery without eager whole-document materialization.
proofLimits: Forty-four selected families were reviewed: 37 Google-facing and seven Plate/Plite platform/lifecycle. Google evidence counts are 19 live-subset, 12 documentation-only, and six unresolved; no complete parity certificate. The machine crosswalk validates 48 unique current Google request union members, including eight explicitly unsupported suggest-mode requests, and 32 unique F-contracts against the 44 audit rows. The original 25 live probes remain one-author, online Chrome/macOS evidence. No new Google document mutation, second-author session, offline replay, real IME, native mobile, assistive-technology run, full format roundtrip, matched Google benchmark, product edit, test suite, or fourth performance trial occurred. The crosswalk proves inventory within its named sources, not implementation or UI parity.
